name: Robust Regression
analogy: Think of it as a jury that listens to every bar but gives less weight to the witness who is shouting. A bar far from the pattern still testifies, but it cannot outvote hundreds of ordinary bars that agree with each other.

steps.title: Fit an ordinary line first
steps.description: It begins with a standard straight-line fit, in which every bar counts equally. This is only a starting point, and it will be pulled toward any extreme bars in the table.
steps.inExample: A first fit on 12 months of 5-minute MNQ bars, including the bars right after scheduled news releases, leans too far because of a few huge reaction bars.

steps.title: Measure how far each bar sits from the line
steps.description: Every bar's miss is recorded and compared with the typical miss. Bars whose miss is far above typical are the suspects.
steps.inExample: A typical bar misses by about 28 points; the bar after the 08:30 jobs report misses by 258 points, nearly ten times typical.

steps.title: Give each bar a weight by how far off it is
steps.description: Bars with small misses keep full weight. Past a chosen threshold, a bar's weight shrinks the further off it is, so its influence is capped instead of growing without limit as it does under ordinary fitting.
steps.inExample: Ordinary bars keep a weight of 100 percent; the jobs-report bar is cut to a weight of 15 percent.

steps.title: Refit the line using the weights
steps.description: A new line is fitted in which each bar counts in proportion to its weight. The extreme bar still has a say, just a small one, and the line settles closer to how the typical bars behave.
steps.inExample: The refit line slopes less steeply than the first one, because the jobs-report bar no longer drags it.

steps.title: Repeat until the line stops moving
steps.description: Because the misses changed after the refit, the weights are recalculated and the line is refit again. This loop usually settles within a handful of rounds.
steps.inExample: After six rounds the weights and the line change by less than a point of forecast, so the loop stops.

steps.title: Forecast, and list the bars that were down-weighted
steps.description: A new bar is forecast with the final line. The list of bars that ended with low weights is a useful by-product: it points to news bars, bad prints and other events worth looking at on their own.
steps.inExample: The 14:35 bar gets its forecast, and the run flags 41 of 61,000 training bars with weights under 30 percent, mostly around scheduled releases.

useFor.example: Estimating how the next-6-bar change in MNQ depends on momentum, without the handful of jobs-report and Fed bars deciding the answer.

useFor.task: A hedge ratio that survives a crash day
useFor.example: Estimating how many ES contracts offset one MNQ contract over a year that includes one violent sell-off bar sequence.

useFor.task: Finding suspect bars in a feed
useFor.example: Listing the bars the fit refuses to trust, such as a stray print far from the surrounding prices, before they reach another model.
Checking which indicators carry a weight distinct from zero when a few extreme bars are not allowed to manufacture the result.

avoidWhen: The extreme bars are the thing you are trying to forecast, such as tail moves around news; down-weighting them throws away exactly that information, and a quantile model speaks about the tails directly.
The data is clean with no real outliers; the robust fit then gives nearly the same answer as an ordinary regression and is slightly less efficient.

example.scenario: A 5-minute MNQ model of the next-6-bar change is fitted on 12 months of bars, including the bars around scheduled news. The robust fit is compared with the weights it assigns to the bars.

input.summary: One row of feature readings for the bar to forecast, plus two training bars that show how the weights work.

fields.name: close
fields.meaning: The price at which the 14:35 five-minute bar closed, rounded to a whole point.

fields.name: change over the last 6 bars
fields.meaning: How much price fell over the previous 30 minutes.

fields.name: distance below the 50-bar moving average
fields.meaning: How far the close sits below its 50-bar average price.

fields.name: volume against its 20-bar average
fields.meaning: How heavy trading in this bar was compared with the recent norm.

fields.name: miss of a typical training bar
fields.meaning: The usual size of the gap between forecast and outcome across ordinary training bars.

fields.name: miss of a jobs-report bar
fields.meaning: The gap between forecast and outcome on one 08:30 news-release bar in the training set.

output.summary: A forecast made with the down-weighted fit, and the weights that explain it.

fields.name: forecast change over the next 6 bars
fields.meaning: The forecast from the robust line, about 12 US dollars per contract before costs.

fields.name: weight of a typical training bar
fields.meaning: Ordinary bars keep full influence on the fit.

fields.name: weight of the jobs-report bar
fields.meaning: The extreme bar is allowed only a small share of influence.

fields.name: training bars with weight under 30 percent
fields.meaning: The count of bars the fit largely refused to trust, listed for review.

example.reading: In this illustration an ordinary fit on the same rows would have given a larger forecast because of the jobs-report bar; the robust forecast reflects how the typical bar behaves. Read the flagged-bar list as a to-do list: confirm they are real events and decide whether to model them separately.
